name: Select
purpose: Pick one option (or several) from a searchable list, shown in a field-styled trigger.
intent: A combobox composed from the pieces the system already has - a TextField trigger, a Dropdown Menu panel, and Chips for multi-select values - preconfigured for the choose-from-a-list use case, rather than a fourth independent implementation of a field, a floating panel, or a token input.
tierNote: Classified as a molecule, but its panel composes Dropdown Menu (an organism, itself Menu + Popup) - the same deliberate, documented exception Tag Group, Avatar Group, Split Button, and Chip already established. See tag-group.contract.json's own tierNote for the full reasoning; not re-derived here. Select also composes two molecules (TextField, Chip), which is ordinary molecule-on-molecule composition.

sourceFiles.note: select.module.css owns the caret's open/close rotation and its colour (content/subtle at rest, content/disabled when disabled - Figma-verified on the trigger's caret_down vector); the trigger frame is TextField's CSS, the panel is Dropdown Menu/Menu's, the chips are Chip's.

figmaSource.note: Filed on the file's own "✅⏲️ Select" page, verified directly against the file via the Desktop Bridge plugin.
figmaSource.structure: One component set, 84 variants across six axes - size (sm/md/lg), tone (default/subtle), state (default/hover/focus/typing/hasValue), inputType (single/multi), isInvalid, isDisabled. Every variant is a `dropdown-menu` instance (Popup + panel) whose trigger slot holds a `figma-parts / select-trigger` (4658:67775), which is itself a `text-field` instance carrying a trailing `caret_down` in its elemAfterInput slot. In multi + hasValue, the trigger's text-field also holds `chip-container` frames (chip-base, mode=select) ahead of the input. The panel's surface slot is the generic empty `panelSurface` in the static file - the real option list is a code decision, the same 'static mockup, real content is code' pattern as every other dropdown-menu-based molecule. Trigger geometry measured per size: sm 32 / radius 8, md 40 / radius 8, lg 48 / radius 12; frame fill color/elevation/surface/raised/default (hover raised/hover), border color/border/input, focus+typing border color/border/focused, disabled background/disabled + border/disabled. The multi trigger is single-line, NO_WRAP at every size - chips sit inline, chip size sm for sm/md triggers and md for lg.

parts.figma-parts / select-trigger: 4658:67775 - 84 variants mirroring select's own axes. Structurally a text-field instance + trailing caret, so the code trigger is the existing TextField molecule, not a bespoke frame.
parts.text-field: The trigger's frame, fill, border, focus/invalid/disabled treatment and per-size geometry are exactly the TextField molecule's - verified token-for-token, so Select reuses TextField rather than restating its state CSS.
parts.caret_down: icon 1496:1775 = the codebase's CaretDownIcon, in the trigger's elemAfterInput slot.
parts.chip-base: multi-select values render as Chips (mode="select") inside the trigger.

apiAdaptationNotes: Props are a discriminated union on `inputType` (default 'single'), so single-select's scalar `value: string | null` and multi-select's `value: string[]` cannot be mixed up - the same pattern Chip uses for `mode`. Single's onChange takes `string | null`; multi's takes `string[]`.

Options are a flat `SelectOption[]` ({ value, label, icon?, description?, disabled?, group? }), not Menu's `MenuSection[]`. Select maps them into sections itself - grouping consecutive options by their `group` field - and owns each row's selected state, selectionType (radio for single, checkbox for multi), and onSelect. This is the ergonomic shape a Select consumer expects; the caller never hand-wires Menu rows.

The trigger is the existing TextField molecule. TextField needed one additive extension - a `leadingContent` slot rendered inside the frame, before the input, NOT aria-hidden (unlike the decorative `iconBefore`) - so multi-select chips render inside the field without a second bordered frame or restating TextField's state CSS. The slot shrinks and clips to keep the field single-line, matching Figma's NO_WRAP trigger. Same 'extend the atom to fill a composition gap' move as Tag's isInteractive and Avatar's entityType.
tone maps to TextField's `appearance` (default/subtle) - Figma names the axis `tone` on the trigger, but it is TextField's appearance axis, so code uses TextField's own name at that boundary.

A11y is the menu pattern, not the strict ARIA combobox/listbox pattern - a deliberate choice matching Figma's own composition (a text input + a dropdown-menu). The input is role=combobox with aria-haspopup=menu and aria-autocomplete=list; the panel is Menu's role=menu with menuitemradio (single) / menuitemcheckbox (multi) rows. Opening keeps focus in the input; ArrowDown moves focus into the Menu, whose existing roving-tabindex takes over; Escape/outside-click close and return focus to the input. A strict listbox (role=listbox/option + aria-activedescendant, focus staying in the input) would not reuse Menu at all and would diverge from how Figma composed it.

Typeahead filtering is Select's own (case-insensitive substring on label) and passed to Menu as pre-filtered sections with showSearch=false - the user chose the trigger itself as the search field over Menu's own built-in search box. A controlled searchValue + onSearchChange hands filtering to the caller (e.g. async loading), in which case Select stops filtering internally.

Multi-select values are removable two ways, matching the confirmed product intent: an ✕ on each Chip (Chip mode=select's own remove button) and re-picking the row in the open menu (checkbox toggles off). Backspace on an empty query removes the last chip. Figma's chip-base shows isRemovable=false, but that is the static mockup state.

The panel always matches the field frame's width and left edge. The trigger child that carries the merged ref + aria-expanded/aria-controls is the inset input (where that a11y wiring belongs), but Select also passes the field frame (the input's parentElement, via a callback ref) as Dropdown Menu's `anchorRef` and sets `matchTriggerWidth`. Popup then measures, positions, width-matches, and scopes its outside-click boundary to the frame - not the ~9px-inset input - and the inner Menu fills that width via `fullWidth`. This keeps the input's single-child trigger + a11y contract intact while the dropdown lines up flush with the visible control. Verified live: panel width and left both equal the frame's on single and multi.
`inputType` is not offered as a runtime-mixable prop; a Select is single or multi for its lifetime, as its value type differs. This mirrors Chip's mode union.

useCases: Choosing one value from a medium-to-long list (status, matter type, assignee)
Choosing several values, shown as removable chips (assignees, tags, practice areas)
Any picker that benefits from type-to-filter over a plain native <select>
antiPatterns: A short, always-visible set of mutually exclusive choices - use Radio
A binary on/off - use Switch or Checkbox
A free-text field with optional suggestions only - use TextField
A menu of actions rather than values - use Dropdown Menu directly

anatomy.name: trigger
anatomy.description: A TextField (role=combobox) - the search input, a trailing rotating caret, and (multi) the selected values as chips inside the frame.

anatomy.name: chips
anatomy.description: multi-select only. One removable Chip (mode=select) per selected value, inside the trigger; sm chips in sm/md triggers, md chips in lg.

anatomy.name: panel
anatomy.description: A Dropdown Menu (Popup + Menu) of option rows - menuitemradio for single, menuitemcheckbox for multi - with an empty message when the query matches nothing.

options.description: The full option list. Each: { value, label, icon?, description?, disabled?, group? }.

value.description: Controlled selection. Scalar for single, array for multi.

onChange.description: Called with the next selection - string|null (single) or string[] (multi).

inputType.description: Discriminates the union. single: radio rows, scalar value, label in trigger. multi: checkbox rows, array value, removable chips in trigger.

size.description: Trigger height 32/40/48; also sets the panel width and chip size.

tone.description: Maps to TextField's appearance - default (bordered) or subtle (bottom-border only).

disabled.description: Disables the trigger; the panel cannot open, and chips render disabled.

invalid.description: Red border and aria-invalid on the input.

searchValue.description: Controlled query. Provide with onSearchChange to filter externally (async); Select then stops filtering internally.

emptyMessage.description: Shown in the panel when the query matches no options.

aria-label.description: Accessible name for the combobox when no visible label is wired by id.

className.description: Composes with the trigger frame's class list.

slots.name: option.icon
slots.allowedContent: Icon or Avatar, decorative - shown in the row and (multi) the chip

single.purpose: One value; radio rows; the chosen label fills the trigger.

multi.purpose: Several values; checkbox rows; removable chips fill the trigger.

accessibility.ariaExpanded: set on the input by Popup, reflecting the panel's open state
accessibility.ariaControls: set on the input by Popup, pointing at the panel while open
accessibility.panelRoles: role=menu with menuitemradio (single) / menuitemcheckbox (multi) rows carrying aria-checked
accessibility.invalid: aria-invalid on the input when invalid
accessibility.focusModel: opening keeps focus in the input; ArrowDown moves into the Menu (its roving tabindex); Escape/outside-click close and return focus to the input
accessibility.note: Deliberately the menu a11y pattern, matching Figma's text-input + dropdown-menu composition, not the strict combobox/listbox + aria-activedescendant pattern - see apiAdaptationNotes.

keyboardInteraction: ArrowDown opens a closed field, or moves focus into the open Menu
Enter / arrow keys / Home / End inside the Menu navigate and activate rows (inherited from Menu)
Backspace on an empty multi-select query removes the last chip
Escape closes the panel and returns focus to the input (inherited from Popup)
behaviorRules: Holds its own open and (uncontrolled) query state; value is always controlled by the consumer.
single: choosing a row calls onChange(value) and closes; the trigger shows the chosen label.
multi: choosing a row toggles the value in the array, keeps the panel open, and clears the query; values render as removable chips.
Filters options itself unless searchValue/onSearchChange are provided, in which case filtering is the caller's.
size sets the trigger height, the panel width, and the chip size together.
disabled blocks opening and disables chip removal.
compositionRules: Pass a flat SelectOption[]; Select builds the Menu sections, selection, and typeahead itself.
Keep option.icon decorative - it appears in both the row and (multi) the chip.
Hold value in the consumer and update it from onChange; Select never mutates selection on its own.
responsiveRules: The trigger stays single-line at every size; multi-select chips shrink and clip rather than wrapping.
The panel inherits Popup's viewport-aware alignment fallback and outside-dismissal.
themeRules: Fully token-driven via the composed components - no light/dark branching of its own. Verified in both themes.

tokens.note: select.module.css references only --fade-quick (the caret rotation transition) and the caret colour tokens --color-content-subtle (rest) / --color-content-disabled (disabled). Every other value belongs to TextField, Chip, or Dropdown Menu/Menu - see their own contract.json files.

do: Give the combobox an accessible name (a wired <label>, or aria-label).
Use single for one choice and multi for several - don't fake multi with repeated singles.
Provide an emptyMessage that names what wasn't found.
dont: Do not pass Menu sections - Select takes a flat option list.
Do not expect a strict ARIA listbox; this is the menu pattern by design.
Do not use Select for a short fixed set of exclusive choices - that's Radio.
acceptanceCriteria: Renders a combobox trigger showing the placeholder when empty and the chosen label (single) when closed.
Opens on click, typing, or ArrowDown; typing filters the options case-insensitively.
single: choosing a row calls onChange and closes, with the row marked aria-checked.
multi: renders a removable chip per value, toggles on re-pick without closing, and removes via chip ✕ or Backspace.
Shows the empty message when the query matches nothing.
Groups options under section headings by their group field.
disabled blocks opening; invalid sets aria-invalid.
size and tone map to the TextField trigger.
Supports a custom id/className on the trigger.
knownLimitations: Menu a11y pattern, not a strict combobox/listbox - screen readers announce a menu, and focus moves into the panel on ArrowDown rather than staying in the input.
The multi-select trigger is single-line; with many values the chips clip - there is no wrap or overflow-count affordance (Figma models none).
Inherits every Menu limitation for the panel (no typeahead-within-menu beyond Select's own filter, no virtualization for very large lists).
futureEnhancements: A clear-all affordance for multi-select, if a real use needs it.
Option virtualization for very large lists.
A strict listbox a11y mode, if a consumer needs combobox/aria-activedescendant semantics.
